original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Do the two E7 receipt representatives still have quadratic ranks 6 and 2, with every single frame-column omission of rank 11, when form_a and form_b are evaluated on the pinned roots?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. PR #5729 published the bit-lane speedup. research/e7-bitslice-coverage-check and research/e7-orbit-hash-partition compared the weight-12 set with the receipt orbits and left the quadratic-rank and single-omission half unreplayed. This package evaluates that half on the two representatives. It does not time the engine or scan the 2^27 kernel.
bottleneck_link: A faster E7 exhaustion is coverage for deletion and decoder checks only when the classified ranks still match the receipt. Checking the two representative forms and their omission ranks closes the half the orbit-hash replay skipped. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after both representative polarizations, both frame-indicator ranks, and all 24 single omissions have been compared with the receipt. Do not rebuild reflection orbits or scan kernel words.
evidence: The pinned polarizations equal diag(1,1,1,-1,-1,-1,0) of rank 6 and the displayed rank-2 product matrix. Each support has frame rank 11. The kernels are one-dimensional with no zero coordinate, so every single omission keeps rank 11. All 24 deleted matrices agree. Four rejecting controls pass. No kernel word is scanned.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does every other word in the two receipt orbits have the same quadratic rank as its representative, or could a reflected support see a different rank?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The receipt assigns one quadratic rank to each orbit. This package checks only the two representative forms, so the rank is not yet replayed on a transported word.
open_questions.first_step: Apply one frozen reflection from source/verify.py to each representative support and evaluate the transported quadratic form on that image.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not call the reflection permutations.

open_questions.question: Does one named decoder code other than the E7 kernel, the E6 frame code, the D6 punctured code, and the P112 weight-16 set satisfy the same half-split equality?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The bit-lane open question asks for another consumer. Those four codes are already recorded by this account, so a fifth consumer would be the remaining coverage step.
open_questions.first_step: Name generators, width and weight bound that are not those four, then compare one half-split with low_weight_words.
open_questions.blocked_by: No fifth consumer is pinned here.
